## The question this category answers

> All members answer: given a yield-bearing position that already exists somewhere else, how do you repackage it into a claim someone else wants to hold — and, critically, who is allowed to decide where the capital goes and under what constraints?

## The category residue the original lane recorded

This category exposes a missing LEVEL, not a missing element, and that is the most important finding in my lane. The vocabulary has elements (mechanisms) and, implicitly, molecules (protocols assembled from them). A STRATEGY is neither: it is a policy expressed OVER molecules — 'borrow USDC on Morpho against stETH up to 80% LTV, unwind if it exceeds 85%, and harvest weekly'. It has no on-chain mechanism of its own; it is a rule for consuming other people's mechanisms. Because the model has no third level, Yearn, Beefy and CIAN decompose to essentially the same two claim symbols ('Sh', 'Ix') plus control-plane furniture, and Steakhouse — with more TVL than the other three combined by a factor of eight — decomposes to the same plus a borrowed 'Im'. The answer to 'is a strategy an element, a molecule, or residue' is: it is residue TODAY, it should not be an element (it is not a mechanism), and the honest fix is a third level with its own primitives — mandate, cap, allocator, rebalancing trigger, performance fee, keeper. Secondary gaps across the category: no auto-compounding/harvest distinct from index accrual; no administered rate; no keeper-liveness dependency; no liquid-wrapper-of-a-locked-position; no maturity-aware pricing; and no way to mark an element as INHERITED from a dependency rather than implemented by the protocol (I hit this with Spark/Ps, CIAN/Ct and Steakhouse/Im/Ct).

### Residue, verbatim

**CIAN Yield Layer** (10):

- that index is written by an off-chain operator at its own discretion, with no oracle input, no attester, no staleness recourse beyond a revert, and no derivation from realised profit and loss
- the vault refuses to report its own assets — and therefore refuses deposits and redemptions — if the index has not been written within three days
- total deposits into the vault are capped at a fixed quantity of the accounting asset
- the vault's assets are deployed as a recursive leveraged loop in an external lending market: supply a staking token, enter its correlated-asset mode, borrow the accounting asset against it, re-stake, repeat
- the ceiling the vault enforces is a self-imposed inner bound below an immutable maximum, and the position is deliberately kept pressed against it
- that agent supplies the leverage amount, the swap route, the slippage floor and the flash-loan source as call arguments; nothing in the contracts computes them, schedules a rebalance, defines when a target has been missed, or compels the agent to act at all
- capital may be forwarded only to strategy contracts the owner has registered with the vault
- no single strategy may hold more than a set fraction of the vault's total assets, checked at the moment of transfer
- the amount a request settles for is decided by the entity that confirms it
- eight per cent of gains is taken by the operator as a performance fee, under a hard ceiling of fifteen per cent, with the documented exit and management fees currently set to zero

**Convex Finance** (10):

- the reward rate on every pooled deposit is multiplied by a boost derived from the protocol's share of a different token's escrowed supply, held by the protocol rather than by the depositor, up to a hard multiple of two and a half
- the governance token of the upstream protocol, when deposited, is added to a single permanent escrow position from which no party can ever withdraw it
- that escrow is re-extended toward its maximum term by any permissionless deposit call whenever it would otherwise begin to decay
- in exchange the depositor receives a transferable token whose only exit is sale on a secondary market, since the position behind it has no redemption function
- voting weight over the escrowed position is non-transferable and is a function of the time remaining on a lock
- lock-holders vote in a proposal on this protocol whose weights are anchored to a historical epoch balance, and a separate executor contract later casts the aggregated result into the foreign protocol's gauge controller through a registered surrogate
- the protocol acquires and exercises governance rights inside four foreign protocols that it does not control
- half a per cent of that revenue is paid to whichever anonymous address calls the harvest function
- arbitrary third-party reward tokens attached to an upstream gauge are forwarded through per-pool stash contracts and virtual-balance children whose balances mirror the parent pool without holding its assets
- no deployed contract's code can be replaced: the protocol commits to immutability and offers shutdown-and-redeploy as its only migration path

**Huma Finance V2** (12):

- the default claim class pays an administered eight per cent annual rate, stated as subject to monthly adjustment at the issuer's discretion
- the holder may switch instantly, for gas only, to a second claim class that pays no cash yield at all
- in exchange the zero-yield class maximises an off-chain point balance which is the holder's entire return
- a depositor may optionally commit for three or six months to multiply that point rate; commitments can be lengthened but never shortened, and breaking one retroactively forfeits the bonus, including on transfer
- redemption is first-come-first-served against a global daily cap that resets at midnight UTC, and requests above the cap are rejected outright rather than queued, against a documented service level of one to seven days
- a holder may bypass the redemption path entirely by selling the claim token into third-party automated market makers
- the yield paid to depositors originates in transaction fees from businesses using an accelerated cross-border payment rail, in practice short-duration advances originated by a single named counterparty
- the redemption round and the price refresh happen only because scheduled off-chain jobs run and call them
- the senior claim may not exceed four times the junior claim, enforced on deposit and again in the ordering of redemptions
- the same address alone sets the borrower's credit limit and the yield in basis points, and may revise both afterwards by raising the limit, changing the yield, extending the term or waiving a late fee
- that address is required to hold junior-tranche capital in the very pool whose credit it underwrites, checked as a liquidity requirement
- the financed obligation is minted as a non-fungible token recording an amount, a currency code, a creation date, a maturity date, a paid amount and a creator, by whoever holds the minting role

**Pendle** (10):

- the accrual index is a monotonic high-water mark: if the source exchange rate falls the yield claim stops accruing entirely, and the drawdown is borne by the principal claim at redemption
- the yield claim's notional shrinks to zero by construction as the remaining accrual window closes
- after maturity the yield claim's index freezes at a snapshot, only already-accrued interest remains claimable, and every reward token subsequently arriving on that expired claim is swept to the treasury
- the principal claim is priced against the wrapper by a pool whose invariant is a logit curve in implied-rate space, whose stiffness parameter grows without bound and whose intercept decays as time-to-expiry shrinks, so identical pool state prices differently on a different day
- the curve's intercept is recomputed before every single trade so that the pre-trade implied rate equals the implied rate left by the previous trade
- the swap fee is quoted as an interest-rate spread whose multiplier is exponential in years-to-expiry, so the same trade pays less notional the nearer maturity is
- anyone may create a new maturity, constrained only to a fixed 24-hour calendar grid, and anyone may create additional markets on an existing principal claim that differ only in curve parameters
- a staker may instead exit immediately by paying a percentage of the staked amount, at a rate the owner may set up to one hundred per cent
- the yield claim accrues off-chain-attested, non-token reward streams from the source protocol, and the same five per cent protocol fee is levied on them
- execution authority over privileged functions is granted per (caller, function selector, target) triple rather than per role or per contract

**Spark Savings (sUSDS / Sky Savings Rate)** (9):

- the interest owed is funded by minting internal protocol debt against the system's surplus/deficit account, unconditionally, with no read of revenue, reserves or any solvency condition
- the rate paid is a written number, not derived from a utilisation curve, an auction or any market; the only bound inside the savings token is that it be non-negative
- the enumerated agent chooses the value of the live savings rate at its own discretion, with no objective function, trigger, target or derivation anywhere in the code
- the agent may write only parameters drawn from an enumerated set of rate identifiers, each with its own configuration record
- the value written must lie between a governance-set floor and ceiling, live two per cent and thirty per cent
- a single update may move the rate by at most a governance-set step, live four percentage points, and no update may occur within a cooldown of the previous one, live sixteen hours; the update then takes effect immediately
- the remote token contains no accrual state and no drip function at all; its value is extrapolated locally from the forwarded tuple and its redeemability is limited by local peg-module inventory rather than by the mainnet balance sheet
- that role may act only through an enumerated set of twenty-nine venue-specific actions — mint, swap, deposit into a named vault, subscribe to a named fund, bridge by a named route — and cannot construct a new one
- each enumerated action carries a maximum amount and a slope that regenerates spent capacity continuously with elapsed time

## Lane narrative

**What the section introduction should say.** Given a yield-bearing position that already exists somewhere else, how do you repackage it into a claim someone wants to hold — and who decides where the capital goes? The corpus called the delegated allocation mandate the most-confirmed gap in the project. This lane sharpens it from a missing element into a primitive with a fixed shape.

**The finding: the mandate has five parts, and every one is residue.**

> named agent → domain whitelist → magnitude cap → rate-of-change limit or delay → revocation

It appears at four of the five targets, always bounding a *different* quantity — leverage, savings rate, venue, credit limit. The code proves the level claim: the reallocation and leverage entry points accept an arbitrary target from a human, and the contract checks only the envelope. Nothing computes the target, schedules a rebalance, defines a missed target, or compels the agent to act at all. **Above all the discretion itself is unnameable.**

**Corrections the lane made to the corpus, with evidence.** One protocol drops both its proxy and its timelock (neither exists) and keeps its emissions symbol only with a note that it pays a thousandth of the rate — which surfaced a new residue: *the vocabulary can name mutability but cannot assert immutability*. One protocol's element set decomposes the institutional product, not the product carrying the capital. One drops emissions entirely, having no token.

**Scale.** The largest object in the category by capital is the one the requirement tables reject, and its distinguishing feature has no symbol at all.
